rewrites.text: The CEO's office is asking the directors to green-light exclusive talks to buy Ferrolake Data Systems, a Rotterdam streaming ingestion startup with 64 employees, at a total enterprise value of as much as 41.5 million dollars.

Our biggest enterprise accounts keep telling us that four hour batch refreshes no longer cut it. Ferrolake has a change data capture engine called Riptrace that pushes warehouse changes through at about 900 ms median latency. Building that ourselves would eat roughly 22 engineer quarters and push our real time dashboards past Q3 2028, whereas buying them lets us ship in Q2 2027.

On price leverage: the target has only about seven months of cash left because it spends near 480k a month. Its last twelve months brought in 6.2M with a 71% gross margin, and existing customers expand by 118% net.

Here is how we would pay: 24M cash on closing from our own balance sheet, 11.5M in our shares priced at 18.40 each (the Series D price), plus up to 6M more over 15 months if Riptrace lands 40 big deployments by the end of 2027.

Biggest worry is keeping the founders. The CTO, Maren Oosterbeek, is the only one who really understands Riptrace's architecture and diligence found the code thinly documented. We would give her 1.1M over three years to stay. Also, two clients making up 38% of Ferrolake's revenue can walk on a change of control, and we have not yet raised it with them.

Raj says 41.5M is the most we would ever pay, not where we start. Open around 34 to 35M and wait for them to ask for more. And we only have management accounts, not audited Q2 figures, so do not trust that 6.2M revenue too much.

Summary: management wants board approval to pursue Ferrolake, a Dutch real-time data startup, for up to 41.5M (cash, stock, earnout), mainly to get Riptrace to market by Q2 2027. Main risks are the CTO leaving and two customers with change of control rights. A rival, Varnetta, may have bid about 35M. LOI requested within 21 days.

TL;DR: we want to buy Ferrolake (64 people, Rotterdam) for no more than 41.5M. It gets us streaming CDC about five quarters faster than building. Watch the CTO retention and the customer consent clauses. A competitor is circling at roughly 35M, so move fast.
Board ask: let us negotiate exclusively with Ferrolake, ceiling 41.5M, open at 34-35M. Rival Varnetta ~35M. Keep the CTO. LOI in 3 weeks.

Imagine our company wants to buy a smaller company that makes a very fast data tool we need. We can pay up to about 41 and a half million dollars, but the plan is to start much lower. Another company wants it too, so we have to hurry.

Ferrolake posted twelve month trailing sales of 6.2 million bucks at a 71 percent gross profit rate and 118 percent net retention of clients. The firm spends about 480,000 dollars a month and holds seven months of cash, giving us substantial bargaining power on the price.

Ferrolake would run as an independent division for two quarters under our VP of Platform. During Q3 2027 we would shift Riptrace to the Calloway control plane and shut down their separate invoicing system, cutting nine duplicate positions in sales ops and finance with severance near 640k.

Ferrolake made six point two million dollars over the last twelve months, with seventy one percent gross margin. It burns four hundred eighty thousand dollars a month and has seven months of runway. The proposed ceiling is forty one point five million dollars.
